content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with meat and vegetables is a restaurant or fast‑food style dish with a thick crust, topped with tomato sauce, a variety of meats (such as ham, sausage, beef) and fresh vegetables (bell pepper, onion, mushrooms, olives). The dough is made from wheat flour, yeast, water and salt, and after baking the crust is crispy on the outside yet soft inside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Italian pizza usually has a thin crust, but thick “deep‑dish” or “pan‑style” versions are popular in the US and Russia.
The combination of meat and vegetables provides a wide range of flavors and makes the dish more nutritionally balanced.
Tomatoes in the sauce contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that remains active even after cooking.
Many restaurants use pre‑mixed dough that is refrigerated for 24–48 hours to improve flavor and crust structure.
Pizza is often served with extra sauces such as garlic, barbecue, or spicy chili sauce.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meats like ham, sausage or beef provide high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables (bell pepper, onion, mushrooms) add vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and folate, supporting immunity and cell function.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The dough and cheese deliver quick‑acting carbohydrates and fats, offering a fast source of energy for active lifestyles.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese (mozzarella, cheddar) supplies calcium important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain crust (when used) add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thick crust, cheese and meat make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Saturated fats and sodium
items.content: Cheese and processed meats can be high in saturated fat and salt, which may negatively affect cardiovascular health if consumed in excess.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Pizza may contain dairy, gluten, and possible additives (soy sauce, spices) that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: If the meat is not fully cooked or the pizza is stored at improper temperatures, there is an increased risk of bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pizza is usually cut into triangular slices and eaten hot; you can add fresh herbs (basil, oregano) or a light drizzle of hot sauce. To reduce calories, replace part of the cheese with a low‑fat option or increase the amount of vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness; a microwave will make the crust soggy.
